To neutralize 28.0 g of hydrochloric acid (HCl), we first determine the moles of HCl using
its molar mass (36.46 g/mol), yielding 0.767 moles. The balanced reaction with calcium
hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂) is: 2 HCl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2 H₂O, indicating a 2:1 stoichiometric
ratio. Therefore, 0.767 moles of HCl requires 0.384 moles of Ca(OH)₂, which corresponds to
28.4 g of Ca(OH)₂ (molar mass 74.09 g/mol). Next, considering the reaction between Ca(OH)₂
and phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄), which follows the equation: 3 Ca(OH)₂ + 2 H₃PO₄ → Ca₃(PO₄)₂ +
6 H₂O, we find that 0.384 moles of Ca(OH)₂ can neutralize 0.256 moles of H₃PO₄. This
results in a mass of 25.1 g of H₃PO₄ (molar mass 98.00 g/mol) that can be neutralized,
demonstrating the application of stoichiometric principles in acid-base reactions.
